title: A controlled experimental evaluation of configuration and cache architecture in LLM serving engines
gist: Much of the reported gap between the two main open engines on a multi-agent workload comes from one default setting, not from architecture.
changes: A warning about every engine-against-engine number here: a single flag explained most of the largest gap. Part of what gets called specialisation is noticing a bad default.
caveats: Only the abstract has been read. A real tail-latency advantage survives at equal throughput, attributed to cache-aware request ordering.

numbers.metric: Share of the largest capacity gap removed by matching one setting

bears_on.note: If one flag is most of the gap, much of the gain from tuning per deployment is available to anyone who reads the documentation.
Comparisons between engines hinge on defaults. Baselines are fragile.
Some of what looks like workload-specific optimum is one setting that was wrong for everyone.
